codex_contract.preserved_semantics: Generate a project-local verification skill that drives the real user surface, records observable evidence, and hands maintenance to a verification loop.

native_mapping.fallback: Missing harness, broken startup, or unavailable native surface preserves the source and returns a blocked verification result.
native_mapping.availability: renderer, isolated verification fixture, and independent local-app fixture evidence checked; live target application and harness not supplied
native_mapping.routing_authority: proof-orchestrator selects the proof path; model-capability-router remains the standing model authority

external_dependencies: target application runtime or supplied harness
permission_gates: Write only to an explicit project-local .agents/skills/verify-<app>/ destination; never write a global skill from this flow.
Run the generated instructions only against an instance started by the verification run, and never kill by process name.
Missing harness or broken startup preserves the source and fails verification.
Do not publish, open a PR, or mutate product code as part of generation without separate explicit authorization.

behavioral_proof.positive: Isolated fixture creates a project-local verification skill, writes its feature files, and preserves the evidence boundary; a separate isolated local-app fixture runner captures independent stdout/exit-code evidence across a pass, induced failure, and correction. Matching map observations remain `FIXTURE_ONLY` because no live target application is driven.
behavioral_proof.missing_tool_or_input: Isolated fixture returns blocked when the verification app is unavailable and performs no product edit.
behavioral_proof.error: Isolated fixture returns an explicit error when supplied feature observations do not match the reconciled map; the local-app failure/correction path is fixture-only and live startup failure remains unproven.

upstream_readme.note: Verified in the pinned upstream clone; the README is referenced for provenance and is not vendored in this skills-only snapshot.

security_review.decision: Keep the source finding and provenance; do not dismiss it because the adapter adds a warning.

codex_note:
## Codex adaptation boundary

This mirror uses the native Codex project-local skill root `.agents/skills/verify-<app>/`. It discovers the real surface from the repository, selects the proof path through proof-orchestrator, and respects the selected model and effort through model-capability-router. The native verification runner is required for a verified result. If the harness or startup is missing, preserve the project and report `blocked`. Generation never installs a global skill, publishes an artifact, opens a PR, kills by process name, or changes product code. The feature-map references intentionally retain the reproducible upstream `control-notes` commands; adapt them to concrete commands observed in the target repository before use. Map browser/Electron/web actions to `cursor-control-ui`, and CLI/TUI actions to `cursor-control-cli`, only when those skills are installed and applicable; otherwise record the exact surface gap. A separate local Python app fixture runner may collect independent stdout/exit-code evidence, but its PASS/FAIL result is not live target verification.
codex_rule: Respect native Codex model/effort, permissions and actual tool availability; no automatic Cursor runtime equivalence.
preserved_requirement: Generate a project-local verification skill that drives your app the way a user does — any language, framework, or platform. Use for /create-verification-skill, "make a control skill for this repo", or when a project has no scripted way to prove UI/CLI/service behavior.
proof: Pinned source hash and deterministic renderer are static provenance. Focused tests render the held candidate, use an isolated project fixture to create a project-local skill, reconcile feature files, and compare supplied observations with a `FIXTURE_ONLY` result. They also run a bounded local Python app fixture and compare independently captured stdout/exit-code evidence across an induced failure and correction. They do not exercise a live harness, target application, or startup failure.
reason: The adapter changes the generated destination and tool boundary while leaving the pinned upstream source unchanged.
